h1: Restroom signs within a clear interior system
lead: Restroom identification is a small part of a building’s sign program with an important practical role. Visitors need to recognize the destination, and the project team needs to confirm the appropriate wording, symbols, tactile elements and placement. Vision Graphics can help New York property teams coordinate the visual design with the wider interior signage. Begin with the approved facilities plan and naming decisions so the final sign schedule reflects the actual rooms and the requirements applicable to the property before production artwork is released.

sections.html: Use the property team’s approved room descriptions and symbols consistently. Avoid making assumptions from an old sign or a generic online example. Where a facility’s use has changed, resolve the naming and design requirements before replacing the panel.

The production proof should record the approved wording and visual treatment, plus any tactile and braille elements. Mounting location and field conditions must also be reviewed. A consistent appearance does not by itself establish that a sign meets the applicable requirements.

items.p: Match the restroom identification to the approved interior sign family.
Prepare tactile and braille elements for professional specification review.
Guide visitors toward facilities from relevant decision points.

items.q: Can a pictogram replace all other information?
items.a_html: The responsible professional should confirm the content and format required for the specific facility and location.

items.q: Can restroom signs match our brand?
items.a_html: Brand colors and styling can be considered within the project’s approved accessibility and identification requirements.
